result.title: XMind: Thinking Twice via Cross-Memory Reasoning for LLM-Based Autonomous Driving
result.summary: Memory-augmented large language model (LLM) driving agents can reuse past experience, yet previously learned corrections often fail to transfer when traffic conditions change. A key limitation is that existing memories mainly record observed outcomes, providing little evidence about alternative actions. We introduce XMind, a training-free framework that enables LLM-based driving to "Think Twice" through cross-memory reasoning. XMind integrates working memory of recent traffic states with episodic memory of critical risk events. The agent first makes an initial decision from the current context and then cross-checks it against retrieved historical experience. If a conflict arises, it makes a second decision guided by the retrieved evidence. To construct reliable episodic memory, XMind evaluates alternative actions through counterfactual rollouts under perturbed traffic conditions and stores the verified outcomes as structured risk capsules. These capsules are retrieved by jointly matching spatial risk patterns and scenario semantics. Across closed-loop highway simulations, XMind achieves success rates of 83.3-93.3%, exceeding the strong baseline by 6.6 percentage points on average. Evaluation on K-Risk further demonstrates lower decision risk on unseen real-world high-risk interactions. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of working memory, risk-text retrieval, and counterfactual verification. Code is available at https://github.com/xiangxiangliuwo/XMind

AI.brief_summary: XMind 是一个免训练的 LLM 自动驾驶框架，结合近期交通状态的工作记忆与关键风险事件的情景记忆：先给出初始决策，再与检索到的历史经验交叉核验，冲突时依据经验做第二次决策；情景记忆由扰动条件下的反事实 rollout 验证后存成结构化风险胶囊，并按空间风险模式与场景语义联合检索。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反事实 rollout 验证备选动作 + 按风险模式检索结构化经验 + 冲突后二次决策」可供核查是否迁移为 latent 假设的生成、证据筛选与再推理/停止机制，但该框架面向驾驶决策且不涉及视觉 latent 状态，联系仍属方法线索。
